pages.lesson:
LESSON: FIELDWORK

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.6: Fieldwork

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Fieldwork. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Explain the main ideas in Fieldwork
2. Practise Fieldwork at school and at home
3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Fieldwork

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Explain the main ideas in Fieldwork
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the main ideas in Fieldwork. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. Practise Fieldwork at school and at home
   In simple words: practise until you can practise Fieldwork at school and at home. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Fieldwork
   In simple words: practise until you can give Kenyan examples connected to Fieldwork. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Fieldwork using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Fieldwork in the examples.
2. Explain Fieldwork to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Fieldwork.
4. Practise one skill from this lesson with a friend.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Fieldwork using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Fieldwork important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Explain the main ideas in Fieldwork
2. Practise Fieldwork at school and at home
3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Fieldwork

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
